questions.question:
Direction: Select the option that is opposite in meaning to the underlined word and mark your answer accordingly.

The government is __persisting__ with its ambitious public works program.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '__**Abandon**__'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word '**Persist**'** **means** ****to continue in an opinion or course of action in spite of difficulty or opposition**.
 
• Marked Option '**Abandon**' in one connotation means **to stop doing an activity before you have finished it**.
 
 
• For example, '*They had to **abandon **their attempt to climb the mountain due to increasing adverse weather and possibility of landslide*.'
 
 
 
• It is clear that '***Persist***' and '**Abandon**' are opposite in meaning.

*Hence, the correct answer is **Option 2**.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Persevere **⇒ continue in a course of action even in the face of difficulty or with little or no indication of success.
 
• **Continue **⇒ persist in an activity or process.
 
• **Endure **⇒ suffer (something painful or difficult) patiently and still exist till the last.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.

Prohibition
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Permission.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ** "Prohibition" **refers to the action of forbidding something, especially by law. (निषेध)

 
 
• ​For example:​The Prohibition era led to the rise of secret speakerships across America.
 
 
 
• **"Permission"** is the antonym of prohibition as it refers to the action of allowing or authorizing something. (अनुमति)
 
 
• **​****For example: **They received permission to hold the event in the public park.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **"Option 4". ** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **"****Restriction"** is similar to "prohibition" in that it means a limiting condition or measure, especially a legal one. (प्रतिबंध)

 
 
• **​****For example:** The library placed a restriction on the number of books one can borrow.
 
 
 
• **"Inhibition"** is a feeling that makes one self-conscious and unable to act in a relaxed and natural way, which could be a result of prohibition but is not its antonym. (नियंत्रण)
 
 
• **​For example:** He overcame his inhibition and spoke in front of the large crowd.
 
 
 
• **"Direction"** does not directly relate to the concept of prohibition or permission in a way that would make it an antonym. (दिशा)
 
 
• **​****For example:** She asked for direction to the nearest gas station.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.

Enchanting
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 4** i.e. **Boring**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"Enchanting"** means something that is delightfully charming or attractive. (मोहक)

 
 
• **Example: **The enchanting music captivated everyone at the concert.
 
 
 
• **"Boring"** refers to something that is not interesting or exciting; it lacks charm or appeal. (उबाऊ)
 
 
• **Example: **The lecture was so boring that many students fell asleep.
 
 
 
• Hence, we can infer that the opposite of **'Enchanting'** is **'Boring'**.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Boring**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Magical** (जादुई): Having the power to make impossible things happen.

 
 
• **Example: **The magician's performance was truly magical and left the audience in awe.
 
 
 
• **Fascinating** (मनमोहक): Extremely interesting and captivating.
 
 
• **Example: **The documentary about space exploration was fascinating to watch.
 
 
 
• **Lively** (जीवंत): Full of life and energy; active and outgoing.
 
 
• **Example: **The lively crowd made the event more enjoyable.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.

Ludicrous
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 2**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"Ludicrous"** means something that is so foolish, unreasonable, or out of place as to be amusing; ridiculous. (हास्यास्पद)

 
 
• **Example: **The idea of flying pigs is utterly ludicrous.
 
 
 
• **"Solemn"** refers to something that is formal and dignified; serious in manner. (गंभीर)
 
 
• **Example: **The event was marked by solemn music and speeches.
 
 
 
• Hence, we can infer that the opposite of **'Ludicrous'** is **'Solemn'**.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 2**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Ridiculous** (हास्यास्पद): Deserving or inviting derision or mockery; absurd.

 
 
• **Example:** His suggestion was so ridiculous that everyone laughed.
 
 
 
• **Antic** (हास्यकर): Grotesque or bizarre.
 
 
• **Example:** The clown's antics were a hit with the children.
 
 
 
• **Farcical** (हास्यास्पद): Relating to or resembling farce, especially because of absurd or ridiculous aspects.
 
 
• **Example:** The whole situation turned into a farcical disaster.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.

Pensive
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Unreflective.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

 

__
 
• The word 'pensive' means **engaged in, involving, or reflecting deep or serious thought**.
 
• **Unreflective**: This term is straightforward - not given to reflection or serious thought. This is a potential antonym of "pensive".

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9074044cf96dc1d09ca89eac99180c3d7440ade1b364d09d47931959bf693cc8.png] **Confusion Points__**

 

__
 
• Frivolous: This word means not having any serious purpose or value, or being carefree and not serious. It can indeed be considered as an antonym of "pensive", which means engaged in, involving, or reflecting deep or serious thought.
 
• **Both "Frivolous" and "Unreflective" can be considered as antonyms for "Pensive". However, if we must select the most appropriate, the choice would be:**
 
• **Unreflective **- as it is the most direct and e**xact opposite of being in a state of deep or serious thought, which "pensive" implies. "Frivolous" could be considered an antonym as well, but it also carries implications of a lack of seriousness or value, which is not inherently present in the definition of "pensive".** Therefore, "Unreflective" would be the most appropriate antonym among the given options.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 

 
• **Hollow: **In terms of describing a person or a statement, "hollow" refers to having no real value, significance, or sincerity, being devoid of substance or character. This doesn't necessarily imply a lack of thought or reflection, it's more about lack of substance or depth. So, this isn't a direct antonym of "pensive".
 
• **Goofy**: This word describes a person who is likely to do silly things, usually in a playful or lighthearted way. Though it might imply a lack of serious thought, it is more about behavior than state of mind, and not a precise antonym for "pensive".

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate antonym of the bold word in the sentence.

We have **accumulated** so much rubbish over the years.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**dissipated**'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word ‘accumulated’(verb) means- "to collect a number or quantity of something over a period of time". (किसी कालावधि में किसी वस्‍तु को अच्‍छी मात्रा या संख्‍या में इकट्ठा कर लेना; संचय करना)

 
 
• *E.g: The company said the debt was **accumulated **during its acquisition of nine individual businesses.*
 
 
 
• *​*Let’s have a look at the meaning of the words that are given in the options:
 
 
• **insinuated**(verb)- “to suggest, without being direct, that something unpleasant is true”. (प्रत्यक्ष हुए बिना सुझाव देना कि कुछ अप्रिय सच है)
 
• **dissipated**(verb)- “to slowly become less until it disappears; to make something weaker until it disappears”. (धीरे-धीरे कम होते-होते ग़ायब हो जाना, समाप्त हो जाना; धारे-धीरे कमज़ोर हो कर ख़त्म हो जाना)
 
• **bristled**(verb)- “used about hair or an animal’s fur, to stand up straight because of fear, anger, cold, etc.”. (डर, क्रोध, ठंड आदि के कारण सीधे खड़े होने के लिए बालों या किसी जानवर के फर के बारे में इस्तेमाल किया जाता है।)
 
• **deviated**(verb)- “to do something that is different from the usual or common way of behaving”. (कुछ ऐसा करने के लिए जो व्यवहार के सामान्य या सामान्य तरीके से अलग हो)
 
 
 
• Therefore, as per the points mentioned above, we find that ‘dissipated’ is the correct antonym of the given bold word.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• The antonyms of the given word 'accumulated' are- 'dissipated', '**contract**', '**divided**', '**scattered**', '**dispersed**', etc.
 
• The synonyms of the given word 'accumulated' are- '**assembled**', '**hoarded**', '**compiled**', '**gathered**', etc.
 
• Example of 'accumulated' in a sentence__: 
 __
 
• *A thick layer of dust had **accumulated **in the room.*
